components.name: CodeBurn
Skyrim Forge
components.note: Developed in this repository at BUNDLED-TOOLS/skyrim-forge; there is no separate SkyrimForge release. The installer resolves ONE versionless install root, migrates a version-stamped install onto it, preserves Workspaces and the virtualenv, wires selected providers, then proves the result runs with `forge doctor`.

components.name: Code Review Skill
components.scope_note: GENERIC languages only (C++, C#, PowerShell, Python, JS...). Skyrim-specific review stays with skyrim-code-review; Papyrus performance stays with papyrus-optimization.

components.name: Obsidian Skills (kepano)
components.scope_note: Markdown/vault/canvas authoring for _AI-SHARED-MEMORY and mod docs. Never used to author Skyrim records or framework INIs.

components.name: claude-mem
components.scope_note: CLAUDE CODE ONLY. Never install for Grok/Codex/Kimi/Hermes. Cross-session CONVERSATION memory (what was done, when, why) — does NOT replace codebase-memory-mcp (code structure graph) or skyrim-memory (verified Skyrim facts). Requires Bun on PATH (worker uses bun:sqlite). Worker port 37777. If red MCP errors: install Bun from https://bun.sh then restart Claude Code.
components.runtime_note: Bun required for worker daemon (https://bun.sh). Without Bun, plugin shows red errors.

components.name: Playwright MCP
components.scope_note: Browser automation for CLIs with no built-in browser. Claude Code already ships a browser pane, so it is skipped there. Never used for Nexus lookups - houseCARL does those keylessly. BROWSER CHOICE: with no flags, playwright-mcp defaults to the Google Chrome channel and prompts you to install Chrome. To use your own browser (Opera GX, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, ...), set user env PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH to the browser exe BEFORE running the installer - the wiring appends --executable-path automatically. Example (Opera GX): setx PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Opera GX\opera.exe". To change later, edit the args in your provider's MCP config (Grok/Codex config.toml, Kimi ~/.kimi-code/mcp.json). Pinned, not @latest: an unpinned npx server can change its tool surface mid-session, and npx will happily reuse a broken cache.

components.name: Firecrawl MCP
components.keyless_skip_reason: Keyless this server is 2 usable tools out of 25 (scrape, search) for 36,321 bytes of schema, ~9,080 tokens on EVERY turn - and those two duplicate the native web tools the providers already have. Not registered without a key; npx resolves this package on first launch, so nothing is cached either way and nothing is lost by waiting until the other 23 unlock. Override with -RegisterKeylessExtras.
components.keyless_note: Measured against the pinned 3.24.0 with FIRECRAWL_* scrubbed, all 25 tools called: exactly TWO work keyless - firecrawl_scrape and firecrawl_search. 21 answer 'Unauthorized: API key is required', including interact, which this note previously listed as keyless. firecrawl_extract is DEPRECATED ('deprecated and unavailable through MCP'), not key-gated. firecrawl_parse needs FIRECRAWL_API_URL pointing at a self-hosted instance, so Firecrawl's own docs saying 'Search, Scrape and Parse' are free do not hold for this server. Regenerate with TOOLS/measure_mcp_capability.py rather than editing by hand.
components.scope_note: Scraping general web docs (CommonLib docs, wikis, GitHub READMEs). NEVER Nexus Mods - houseCARL reads Nexus keylessly with changelogs and file lists.

components.name: Perplexity MCP
components.scope_note: REQUIRES PERPLEXITY_API_KEY (paid). Not installed on a keyless machine. Current-information research (new SKSE/CommonLib releases, game patch news). Never a substitute for houseCARL on Nexus, codebase-memory on code, or skyrim-memory on verified Skyrim facts.

components.name: GitHub MCP Server (official)
components.scope_note: GitHub's official server, replacing @modelcontextprotocol/server-github, which npm marks 'Package no longer supported'. Registered with a scoped --toolsets list, not 'all': the server exposes 20 toolset groups and every enabled group costs tool-schema tokens on every turn. Widen it per project, never globally.

components.name: Serena
components.scope_note: Language-server-backed symbol search and editing. NOT registered globally and NOT registered machine-wide: TOOLS\Set-McpProfile.ps1 wires it for the one project that shows source-tree markers, because every connected server's tool schemas ride in context on every turn of every session that config covers. Claude Code takes it in projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers, Grok in the project's own .grok\config.toml; Codex, Kimi and Hermes have no project-scoped MCP config and are skipped unless -Global is passed. Registered with a per-client --context so the tool set is trimmed to what the client does not already provide -- Serena 1.7.0 ships one for claude-code, codex and grok, and Kimi/Hermes fall back to the generic 'agent' context -- and with --project <path> so it activates the project it was written for. Overlaps codebase-memory-mcp deliberately: that answers 'where is this in the graph', this answers 'what does this symbol resolve to, and rewrite its body'.

components.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
components.scope_note: Reads a live Chrome: console, network, performance traces, rendered DOM. The half playwright-mcp does not do -- playwright drives a browser, this explains what the browser did. Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing only; Chromium forks are not supported by this server, unlike playwright-mcp which takes PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH. --no-usage-statistics opts out of Google's telemetry, which is on by default upstream; this pack does not enable third-party telemetry on a user's machine without asking.

components.name: shadcn registry MCP
components.scope_note: Resolves registries from the project's components.json, so it is meaningless outside a shadcn project and is written project-scoped only.

components.name: Blender MCP
components.scope_note: Talks to an addon inside a running Blender. Pinned: `uvx blender-mcp` was version-free through 7.9.6, and an unpinned invocation can change its tool surface mid-session. `uvx blender-mcp@1.8.3 install-addon` places the addon, but ENABLING it is inside the editor and cannot be done from outside that process -- so the profile prints the step rather than claiming it ran it. Note the difference between 'the MCP executable starts' and 'the addon is connected': the server answers initialize with no Blender running at all, and only a tool call that reaches the scene proves the second. Blender is discovered from %APPDATA%\Blender Foundation, which Blender creates on first run whatever the install source -- 7.9.6 carried a maintainer's own Steam drive path here, which could never match on another machine. Telemetry: the addon has a consent-gated `telemetry_consent` preference and no telemetry endpoint; it is off unless the user enables it inside Blender, where this pack cannot reach it.

components.name: Godot MCP
components.scope_note: Shells out to the Godot editor binary, which has no fixed install location on Windows, so the profile is gated on GODOT_PATH: setx GODOT_PATH "C:\path\to\Godot.exe".

components.name: Unity MCP
components.scope_note: There is no machine-wide Unity MCP server. The executable is generated inside the project's Library folder by the Unity package, so the entry is project-scoped by construction and its command is the resolved absolute path for that one project. Until the package is installed the exe does not exist, and the profile refuses rather than writing a path that is not there.

dotnet8-sdk.note: Needed to build/run Spooky from source

notes: Multi-provider Ultimate AI Starter Bundle. Includes optional full Skyrim SE/AE modding stack; not Skyrim-only.
spec_notes: MCP servers in this pack are local stdio; the 2026-07-28 stateless spec requires no change to them. Components carrying a 'profile' are NOT registered by the installer, and since 7.9.6 are not registered machine-wide either: BUNDLED-TOOLS/PROFILES.json holds their wiring and TOOLS/Set-McpProfile.ps1 applies a profile to ONE project -- the one whose markers asked for it -- when the machine satisfies its requirements. MCP tool schemas are in context on every turn, so a machine-wide registration is a permanent cost paid by every unrelated session; measured on a real machine, eight connected servers were 188 tool schemas per turn. Project scope means projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers in ~/.claude.json for Claude Code and <project>/.grok/config.toml for Grok; Codex, Kimi and Hermes have no project-scoped MCP config, so they are skipped with the reason printed rather than written machine-wide. Prove any registration with TOOLS/Test-McpHandshake.ps1.
